subtopics.content: Early computing devices to modern computers, hardware/software constituents, data vs information, security threats and legal issues
subtopics.objective: Trace computing history from Abacus/Babbage to ENIAC/UNIVAC and modern PCs/palmtops; differentiate hardware/software and data/information; identify security threats (viruses, hackers, cybercrimes) and preventive measures (antivirus, firewalls, encryption); examine software copyright and digital privacy.

topics.title: Computer Hardware, Logic Circuits, and System/Application Software

subtopics.content: Input/output devices, CPU/Memory units, storage conversions, logic gates (AND/OR/NOT/NAND/NOR), operating systems, translators, application packages
subtopics.objective: Classify input/output devices; understand CPU (ALU, Control Unit) and memory types (RAM, ROM, auxiliary storage units/conversions); construct truth tables and logic gate equations; differentiate system software (OS, compilers, interpreters, utilities) and application software (GUI vs command line OS).

topics.title: Computer Applications (Word Processing, Spreadsheet, Database, Graphics, Presentation)

subtopics.content: Operations and features of MS Word, MS Excel, MS Access, CorelDraw, and MS PowerPoint
subtopics.objective: Master editing, formatting, and file operations in MS Word; perform spreadsheet cell calculations, formulas, functions, and charting in MS Excel; build database structures, tables, queries, and reports in Access/DBMS; design graphic cards/logos in CorelDraw; create animated slide shows in PowerPoint.

topics.title: Managing Computer Files and Basic Computer Operations

subtopics.content: File structures, organization/access methods, file security, booting, computer data registers/buses
subtopics.objective: Define data items, records, files, databases, and file organizations (serial, sequential, index, random); identify causes of data loss and security methods (backups, passwords); differentiate cold/warm booting; explain data processing cycle, registers (MDR, CIR), and bus width transfer factors.

topics.title: ICT, Internet, Networking, and World Wide Web

subtopics.content: ICT applications, internet browsers, e-mail management, network topologies/devices, web protocols (HTTP/HTML)
subtopics.objective: Understand ICT broadcasting, telecommunications, and applications (teleconferencing, ATM, POS); navigate web browsers, search engines, and manage e-mail accounts; classify networks (PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN) and topologies (Star, Bus, Ring); understand web development protocols (HTTP, HTML) and website navigation; identify network cables (twisted pair, fibre optic) and connectors (RJ45, USB).

topics.title: Problem-Solving Skills, Programming Languages, BASIC, and Systems/Program Development

subtopics.content: Programming levels, algorithms, flowcharts, BASIC statements/arrays, system development life cycle, program compilation
subtopics.objective: Compare Machine, Low Level, and High Level languages; write algorithms and construct flowcharts; execute BASIC statements, arithmetic expressions, built-in functions, and 1D arrays; detail the stages of the Systems Development Cycle; explain steps in the Program Development Cycle (coding, debugging, documentation).
